summary: A wooden Victorian lighthouse above San Luis Obispo Bay, lit in 1890 for Port Harford; automated in the 1970s and restored by volunteers, now open on guided tours.

lens.where: horn house visitor center at the station (returned 2010)

access.note: Reached by docent-led Pecho Coast Trail hike or tours run by the Point San Luis Lighthouse Keepers; not open for walk-in visits.

notes_for_editor: No LHB reports for 1887-1890 in the corpus, so construction details rest on the NRHP and Lighthousefriends (facts only, own words). Roster is the USLHS list, not checked against a primary register; William J. Smith was head keeper in 1916 per the archive but Lighthousefriends calls the rescuing keeper 'W.M. Smith', so the story does not name him. The Commissioner's 1916 table is in columns: the Roanoke entry was matched to San Luis Obispo by position (W. M. Greene, second assistant keeper, San Luis Obispo appears in that block), please check the page image. Fiscal years: 1893/1894/1895 fog hours are for the fiscal years ended June of those years. Newspaper search (Chronicling America, Roanoke/Port Harford 1916) returned nothing. Shows 1969 lens change vs 1975 deactivation vs 1974 automation from different sources. Fact-check 2026-10-22: Commissioner 1916 p.62 page image read; entry is W. M. Greene, second assistant keeper, San Luis Obispo (matches roster); Lighthousefriends names Keeper W.M. Smith, so the story states the discrepancy.
